title: Design parity: port numbered Pager (replace Load more) on profile feed
description:
Port the old app's Pager over the "Load more" button in apps/web.

The old Ratat app paginates feeds with a numbered pager; the new app's profile feed (apps/web/src/routes/profile.$handle.tsx) uses a "Load more" button, which is a design-parity violation.

Port from /home/answer/Workspace/ratat/apps/frontend:
- src/components/Pager.tsx (top/bottom/standalone variants, settings cog with "Always show details" toggle driving body.show-details, page-number nav with gaps, Prev/Next/Last, "N works" count) — transcribe the JSX/classes 1:1, adapting Next.js Link/usePathname/nuqs to TanStack Router equivalents (Link, useLocation, search params via route validateSearch). Drop captureEvent (no observability lib here yet) rather than porting telemetry.
- src/lib/pagination.ts (pagerLinks, formatTotal, slot/gap computation, capped totals) and the relevant parts of use-pager.ts / search-params.ts (?page= handling).

Cursor mapping: the Bluesky appview getAuthorFeed is cursor-based, not offset-based. Approach: keep page size fixed (match the old app's limit), treat the profile's postCount as the (capped) total for computing page slots, and resolve page N by walking cursors server-side in art.ratat.feed.getAuthorFeed (accept a page or cursor param as appropriate) or client-side caching of cursors per page — choose the simplest correct approach and note it in the close reason. Prev/page-number navigation must work for pages already visited at minimum; document any deeper limitation as a follow-up bd issue.

Use the pager on the profile Art tab (top and bottom, like the old app's ProfileFeed/ProfileFeedTab usage — check those files for exact placement and countNoun). Remove the Load more button.

Gates: just check green, bun run build green. Verify in dev against a real handle (e.g. bsky.app) that page navigation renders distinct pages.
close_reason:
Ported the old app's numbered Pager onto the profile Art tab, replacing the Load more button.

Frontend: apps/web/src/components/Pager.tsx and apps/web/src/lib/pagination.ts are 1:1 transcriptions of the old app's files (same markup, classes, slot/gap maths, formatTotal, top/bottom/standalone variants, settings cog with the 'Always show details' toggle driving body.show-details). Three adaptations: cva folded into the repo's cn() helper (no class-variance-authority dependency here), Next Link/usePathname/nuqs replaced by TanStack Link plus route validateSearch/loaderDeps on ?page=, and captureEvent dropped. Page slots carry TanStack LinkProps instead of serialized hrefs, matching the TabNav pattern. The pager Links get activeOptions={exact, includeSearch} — otherwise the router marks the page-1 link active on every page (search params match by subset) and emits a second aria-current in the nav. Added body.show-details rules to styles.css (ported from the old globals.css) so the toggle actually does something, and re-exported SettingsIcon from lucide.

Cursor mapping (server-side walk, chosen over client-side cursor caching): art.ratat.feed.getAuthorFeed gained a 'page' param (1..100) and a 'page' output field. The handler walks upstream cursors to the requested page and returns the page it reached. A per-process cursor cache (apps/xrpc-server/src/cursor-cache.ts, 5 min TTL, 5000 entries) records the cursor that starts each page as the walk passes it, so Next/Prev/revisits and any page a previous walk crossed cost one upstream request; only a cold deep jump costs one request per page. Chosen because it keeps the frontend stateless — every page is a plain link that works on direct load, SSR, and back/forward — which client-side cursor caching cannot do.

Totals: page slots are sized from the profile's postsCount (an upper bound, since text-only posts are counted but non-media posts are dropped from the feed) and rendered capped as 'N+ works'. Walking past the end of a feed returns its last page, and the output 'page' field lets the client clamp the pager to the page actually served, replace the estimate with the exact count, and drop Next/Last. Verified in dev against bsky.app: pages 1/2/3 render distinct posts; ?page=7 and ?page=27 land on the real last page (6), highlight 6, show '169 works' exactly, and disable Next.

Gates: just check green, bun run build green.

title: Design parity: copy old-app page designs 1:1 (login fix, masthead, square corners, profile page)
description:
Design parity pass: make every existing page in apps/web match the OLD Ratat app's design 1:1.

Context: Phase 1 shipped functional pages (login, /profile/$handle, lightbox) but with an invented design. The user wants the old app's design copied literally — layout, CSS, spacing, typography, component styling — not reinterpreted. Old repo (reference source of truth): /home/answer/Workspace/ratat/apps/frontend — its globals.css, components/, and app/ pages.

Required fixes (user-reported):
1. Login page styling is BROKEN: the whole page renders compressed into a tiny column (text wrapping one word per line, tiny input/button). Likely Tailwind v4 source scanning/content detection not picking up utilities, or a container/preflight issue. Diagnose and fix the root cause first, then style the login page to match the old app's sign-in design.
2. Header/masthead must match the old app's masthead exactly (structure, spacing, typography, nav placement).
3. Buttons, inputs, and dialogs must NOT be rounded — copy the old app's exact border-radius/border/spacing styles. Audit all interactive elements for parity.
4. Profile page must copy the old app's profile page design one-for-one: same ProfileHeader layout, same grid presentation (.piece/.masonry patterns from the old globals.css @layer components — see issue ratat-app-cso; port those component styles now since real components exist). NO hover zoom-in effect. NO click-popup detail dialog unless the old app does exactly that — replicate the old app's artwork detail interaction instead (check how CollectionView/artwork cards/detail pages work in the old repo and mirror it).
5. General rule going forward: page designs are PORTED from the old app, never invented. When the old app has no equivalent page, stay maximally consistent with its visual language.

Method: for each page/component, open the old repo counterpart (components like ProfileHeader.tsx, FollowingRail.tsx, ui/*, globals.css layers) and transcribe the JSX structure + classes, adapting only what routing/data differences require. Keep the light-dark() token system; the old repo uses the same tokens so classes should mostly transfer directly.

Quality gates: just check green, bun run build green. Visually verify by running the dev server and checking the login page renders full-width and correctly styled (e.g. screenshot or DOM inspection via curl of rendered HTML for sanity).

Close ratat-app-cso too if you port the @layer components styles as part of this.
close_reason:
Every page in apps/web is now transcribed from /home/answer/Workspace/ratat/apps/frontend.

ROOT CAUSE of the broken login page: not source scanning. The ported theme defines --spacing-md: 12px, and Tailwind v4 resolves max-w-* from both --container-* and --spacing-*, so .max-w-md compiled to max-width:12px and squeezed the page into a 12px column (verified in the built CSS). Fixed by dropping the t-shirt width utilities in favour of the old app's .wrap plus explicit pixel widths. Filed a follow-up to guard the collision.

1. Login: new /login route, a literal port of the old sign-in card — 380px bordered panel, header strip in bg-header with the 2px header-edge rule and BrandMark, square input with the accent focus ring, btn btn--accent Continue. Screenshotted at 1280px: full width, correct.
2. Masthead: old structure exactly — sticky bg-header, border-b-2 header-edge, .wrap flex h-[42px] gap-18, BrandMark 'ᓚᘏᕐᐷ Ratat', MastheadNav, centred search frame, AuthControl (Sign In btn signed out; 28px square avatar + square dropdown signed in). Footer ported too.
3. Square corners: .btn has border-radius 0; every input, dialog, menu, card and avatar uses the old app's borders and spacing. The like consent popover is now a bordered panel, not a rounded card. lint:colors green.
4. Profile: ProfileHeader ported one-for-one (clamp banner with the contrast gradient, clamp avatar with inset ring, overlay name/handle chips, stats row, ghost action button, TabNav) over the .gallery/.wrap.layout/.feed shell; grid is .masonry/.piece. No hover zoom — hover reveals the artist bar and action bar exactly like the old app (verified by screenshot).
   The click-popup lightbox is deleted. The old app navigates to a detail page, so /art/$handle/$rkey now mirrors ArtworkDetail: framed image, title, artist row, favourite button, description/meta panel with the Bluesky chip, 'More by' sidebar rail.
   Backing that route needed a read query, so this also adds art.ratat.feed.getPost (actor + rkey) with an xrpc-server route; postView was split into artworkView for the non-feed case. Verified live against the Bluesky appview.
5. CLAUDE.md already records the port-never-invent rule.

Also added: lucide-react for the old icon set, lib/utils cn, lib/avatar, lib/date, lib/artwork-href, DevLoopbackRedirect (moved out of the home route).

Gates: just check green, bun run build green. Verified in a browser at 1280px — login, home, profile, hover state, artwork detail.

Left out, with follow-ups filed: Following nav + real SearchBar, the other profile tabs and ProfileSidebar, comments/tags/collections/boost on the detail page, and a lint guard for the spacing/container token collision.

title: Phase 3: art.ratat.graph.follow lexicon, home feed, import-follows onboarding
description:
Full plan: .hermes/plans/2026-08-05_ratat-lens-migration.md (Phase 3 section + Decisions). Old repo reference for DESIGN ONLY: /home/answer/Workspace/ratat/apps/frontend — port page/component designs 1:1 per CLAUDE.md (square corners, old layout; never invent designs). Old home/following pages and FollowButton styling are the visual reference.

Goal: the ratat social graph and the logged-in home feed.

Scope:
1. Lexicon `art.ratat.graph.follow` (record: subject did, createdAt) + codegen. This is the ONLY custom record lexicon in the app.
2. FollowButton on profile pages (and wherever the old design had it): logged-in users write/delete art.ratat.graph.follow records in their own PDS via com.atproto.repo. Follow state hydrates from the local index (fall back to listRecords for the viewer's own repo if not yet indexed).
3. Ingest ratat follows: jetstream tail already runs — add art.ratat.graph.follow creates/deletes (scoped by DID? No — like likes, followers can be anyone; but we only care about follows FROM any DID TO anyone, and follows live in the follower's repo. Subscribe to the collection globally — volume will be tiny since only ratat users write it). Store in ratat_follow table (follower did, subject did, rkey, createdAt). A ratat-follow arriving marks the SUBJECT DID interested (plan: interested-set trigger (c)) and enqueues backfill.
4. Backfill the viewer's existing follows on login if their repo has art.ratat.graph.follow records not yet indexed (listRecords walk).
5. Home feed: `art.ratat.feed.getTimeline` (new query lexicon) — reverse-chron media posts from the viewer's ratat-follows, served from the local index, page-number pagination like getAuthorFeed. Logged-out home stays the pure login page. Logged-in home = the feed, designed 1:1 from the old app's home page (grid + pager).
6. Onboarding import-follows step: after first login (viewer has zero ratat-follows), offer the user's Bluesky follow graph (app.bsky.graph.getFollows walk) as initial ratat-follows; user confirms; write via com.atproto.repo.applyWrites in batches of up to 200 creates per call. One-time offer, dismissible, no ongoing sync. Design: port the old onboarding step's look where applicable.
7. Keep frontend Effect-free; backend all Effect; colors via light-dark() tokens.

Constraints: no posting/uploads/boosts; likes unchanged; do NOT push to remote; no narrating comments.

Gates: just check green, cd apps/web && bun run build green, and real end-to-end verification: log in (or simulate with a test account if OAuth interactive login is impractical headlessly — then verify the write path with curl/agent calls against the real PDS only if safe; otherwise verify follow ingest by writing a record via the app and watching psql), confirm ratat_follow rows appear via jetstream, confirm home feed serves followed actors' media posts from the index, confirm import-follows batching logic with a dry-run/unit test. Document verification results in the close reason.
close_reason:
Shipped in 5 commits (8050a91, 179e86d, 898f88e, 42fbfa8, d41ab2e).

WHAT WAS BUILT
- Lexicons: art.ratat.graph.follow was already defined; added art.ratat.feed.getTimeline (viewer, limit, page → feed + page + total) and art.ratat.graph.getFollows (actor, limit, cursor → follows + indexed flag). Codegen run.
- Index: ratat_follow table (uri pk, did, rkey, subject, createdAt) plus follows_wanted_at / follows_backfilled_at / follows_backfill_attempted_at on actor, mirroring the post-backfill columns. Migration 0001 applied.
- Ingester: third jetstream subscription on art.ratat.graph.follow, unscoped like the like tail but nearly free since only Ratat writes the collection. A follow marks its SUBJECT interested (trigger (c)), fetching their profile once for a handle. Second worker walks com.atproto.repo.listRecords on the actor's own PDS (resolved through the DID doc) for follows written before the tail existed; queued by follows_wanted_at, which getFollows/getTimeline stamp.
- xrpc-server: getTimeline joins post against the viewer's follows, page-number offsets, no live fallback (a timeline is a join over a graph only we hold). getFollows serves the records and reports indexed=false until the walk has run.
- Web (Effect-free): lib/graph.ts writes follows to the viewer's PDS (createRecord/deleteRecord, applyWrites in batches of 200 for the import, listRecords for own-repo reads, app.bsky.graph.getFollows for the offer); FollowsProvider holds the viewer's graph once (index first, own repo as fallback, local mutation after writes); FollowButton ported 1:1 from the old app (default variant on the profile header, compact variant on the artwork detail, as the old design had); home is the sign-in card logged out (LoginPanel shared with /login) and the old home's pager+masonry+pager over getTimeline logged in; /onboarding is the old ImportStep ported to people, offered once after login, dismissible.
- docs/architecture/indexing.md updated with the Ratat graph, the follow tail, the timeline read and the queue limit.

GATES
- just check green (lint, lint:colors, format:check, typecheck across all 6 packages).
- cd apps/web && bun run build green.
- bun run test: 14 tests, 0 fail (9 web + 5 ingester).

END-TO-END VERIFICATION (real network, real Postgres on 5433)
- Graph walk against a real PDS: GET art.ratat.graph.getFollows?actor=ansxor.ca stamped follows_wanted_at; the worker resolved the DID doc, walked nest.ansxor.ca and wrote 7 ratat_follow rows over 5 distinct subjects (log: 'graph backfill did:plc:brka7... 7 ratat follow(s)'). Duplicate follows of one subject were tolerated as designed.
- Interested-set trigger (c): all 5 subjects were inserted with correct handles (chex.zone, shimzo, apolozorua, lynasdf, haloopdy) and then backfilled by the post worker to 929 artworks total.
- Home feed from the index: getTimeline?viewer=ansxor.ca returns 929 total, reverse-chron across the followed artists with bylines and CDN media; page=2 returns a distinct page; page=9999 clamps to page 31 with 29 items (929 = 30x30+29).
- getFollows after the walk: indexed=true, 7 follows, no cursor.
- Follow tail: subscription established ('[jetstream:follows] subscribing collections=art.ratat.graph.follow dids=all cursor=live'). No live event could be produced (only this project writes the collection and the records predate jetstream retention), so the handler was driven directly against real Postgres with a synthetic commit: create wrote the row, delete removed it, count back to 7. Event routing (create/delete/no-subject/other-collection/identity) covered by 5 unit tests with a recording Database layer.
- Import batching: 9 unit tests against a fake PDS fetch handler — 450 subjects become 3 applyWrites calls of 200/200/50, each write a com.atproto.repo.applyWrites#create of art.ratat.graph.follow naming its subject; progress callbacks 200 then 250; empty selection writes nothing.
- Web: SSR + hydration checked in a real browser — logged-out home hydrates to the sign-in card with no console errors, /onboarding SSRs its guard state, profile page still renders header, grid and numbered pager.

NOT VERIFIED: creating/deleting a follow through the app itself, and the import running for real, both of which need an interactive OAuth login that was not available headlessly. Filed as ratat-app-4ya.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: ratat-app-c3m (backfill queue is FIFO — a 26,521-artwork walk held it for over two minutes and delayed freshly followed artists; worked around by hand during verification), ratat-app-4ya (browser verification of the write path), ratat-app-0k6 already covers post re-walks and a new sibling covers re-reading a follow graph after the one-off walk.

Not pushed.

title: Phase 2: Postgres index, interested-set, lazy backfill, jetstream tail
description:
Full plan: .hermes/plans/2026-08-05_ratat-lens-migration.md (Phase 2 section + decisions). Old repo reference: /home/answer/Workspace/ratat (docs/architecture/indexing.md and bluesky-mirroring.md describe the old model — the new one is much smaller).

Goal: introduce the local Postgres index so Ratat stops hammering the public appview on every request, while keeping the live-fetch path as fallback. The index answers only "which posts/actors do we know about"; profile stats still hydrate live from public.api.bsky.app at read time; like counts are MIRRORED into the index (see scope 4b).

Scope:
1. Schema in packages/db (Drizzle): actor table (did, handle, displayName, avatar/banner refs, description, interested_at, backfilled_at, indexed_at) and post table (uri, did, rkey, createdAt, media JSONB matching the lexicon media views, text, indexed row timestamps). Identify by DID. Real Drizzle migrations runnable via just migrate. Consider issue ratat-app-9wz (Effect Database layer in packages/db) — implement it as part of this if it fits naturally; claim/close it too if done.
2. Interested-set: marking a DID interested happens on (a) profile visit, (b) login, ((c) ratat-follow arrives in Phase 3). When a not-yet-interested profile is first visited, mark interested and enqueue backfill.
3. Backfill worker (apps/ingester, Effect): for each interested DID with backfilled_at null, walk getAuthorFeed(posts_with_media) via the public appview to a sane depth (all pages; respect rate limits with a polite delay), upsert media posts (including likeCount seeded from the appview feed response), set backfilled_at. No reposts, no text-only posts.
4. Jetstream tail (apps/ingester, Effect): subscribe to jetstream (wss://jetstream2.us-east.bsky.network or configurable) filtered to app.bsky.feed.post creates/deletes, app.bsky.feed.like creates/deletes, and identity/profile updates; index post events only from interested DIDs; upsert/delete accordingly. 4b (DECIDED 2026-08-06): like events increment/decrement a like_count column on the post row when the liked subject URI is a post we index (likes can come from ANY DID, not just interested ones — filter by subject, not author). Reads serve the mirrored count; no per-read appview hydration for counts, and no per-liker records stored. Store cursor for resume.
5. xrpc-server reads: getAuthorFeed / getPost serve from the local index when the DID is backfilled; otherwise serve live from the public appview (current behavior) while marking interested. Page-number pagination should now be offset-based over the local index when indexed (cheaper than cursor walking).
6. Keep art.ratat.* lexicon surface unchanged unless a field is genuinely needed.
7. Write docs/architecture/indexing.md documenting the interested/backfill/tail model (fresh doc, new model — do not copy the old one).

Constraints: backend all Effect; like COUNTS are mirrored (seed + jetstream tail) but no liked-by/per-liker data; no blob storage — media stays as CDN URLs; frontend should not need changes beyond whatever the swap to indexed reads requires (ideally none). docker-compose Postgres on port 5433 already exists; just up / just migrate work.

Gates: just check green, bun run build green, and a real end-to-end verification: start Postgres + ingester, visit/mark an interested DID (e.g. bsky.app), watch backfill populate rows (verify with psql counts), restart xrpc-server, confirm profile page serves from index (log line or timing), and confirm jetstream tail inserts a new post from a busy interested account if observable. Document verification results in the close reason.
close_reason:
Phase 2 landed in 1689a0e. The local Postgres index, the interested set, the lazy backfill worker and the jetstream tail all work end to end against live Bluesky.

WHAT SHIPPED
- packages/db: actor, post, post_like, ingestion_cursor; real drizzle migration (0000_polite_paper_doll.sql) applied via just migrate. Effect Database layer (ratat-app-9wz, closed).
- packages/common: CDN URL construction and media extraction from both an appview embed view and a raw firehose record — verified to produce byte-identical URLs to the appview's own.
- apps/ingester: serial backfill worker (politeness delay, back-off, error recorded on the actor row) and two jetstream subscriptions with resumable cursors.
- apps/xrpc-server: index-first getAuthorFeed and getPost; page numbers are offsets over post_author_feed_idx with a base64url keyset cursor; interest marked on every read path.
- docs/architecture/indexing.md: fresh doc for the new model, its limits and its knobs.
- No lexicon changes. No frontend changes.

VERIFICATION (live, against public.api.bsky.app and jetstream2.us-east)
- just check green; bun run build green.
- Interest marking: GET art.ratat.actor.getProfile?actor=bsky.app created the actor row with interested_at set. A getAuthorFeed for a never-seen actor also marked it, from the byline of the first post fetched, at no extra upstream cost.
- Backfill: bsky.app -> 168 artworks across 2 pages, backfilled_at stamped. Later actors up to 5200+ posts walked the same way. Final state: 14 actors, 68145 posts.
- Indexed reads after an xrpc-server restart (cold cursor cache): page 1 12ms, page 4 3.8ms, getPost 4ms. Same page 4 served live for an unindexed actor: 717ms (4 upstream requests). Page-past-the-end clamps correctly (asked page 100 of 71, served 71). A cursor taken from page 8 returns exactly page 9's first post, so keyset and offset paging agree. Unknown handle still returns ProfileNotFound.
- Jetstream post tail: confirmed inserting live, e.g. at://did:plc:ctgmt7vyh57ylh6lunlbe3q5/app.bsky.feed.post/3msgh3uame52t indexed at 16:44:29 for a post created at 16:20, media stored as a real jsonb array with correct CDN URLs.
- Jetstream like tail: 197 like records counted across dozens of indexed posts, with post.like_count and updated_at moving. A like on a bsky.app *text* post correctly no-opped, which is applyLike's 'where exists' guard doing its job.

DEVIATION FROM THIS ISSUE'S TEXT — LIKE COUNTS
The issue says 'no mirroring of likes (counts stay live)'. The plan file was edited mid-implementation with a decision dated 2026-08-06 that reverses this: like_count is mirrored, seeded at backfill and maintained from a jetstream like tail. I treated the dated plan decision as the newer authority and implemented it, but the cost is worth stating plainly, because it is not what 'cheaper at scale' suggests: a like lives in the *liker's* repo, so the subscription cannot be scoped by DID the way the post tail is. It is the entire app.bsky.feed.like firehose, measured at ~210 events/second, every one decoded and thrown away. Local filtering is cheap (one at-uri parse plus a set lookup) but the bandwidth is not. JETSTREAM_LIKE_TAIL=false turns it off. Filed for a measured decision.

Two consequences of that decision that the plan did not anticipate:
- A like *delete* arrives with no record and therefore no subject, so a mirrored counter cannot be decremented without storing something. post_like maps a like URI back to its post, for likes on indexed posts only. This is narrower than the plan's 'no per-liker records stored' but is the only way the counter converges.
- reply_count and repost_count are frozen snapshots from backfill time; maintaining them would need two more global tails. Filed separately.

BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION
- A missing DATABASE_URL made every read 500 instead of falling back to live. DatabaseLive is now typed with DbError and xrpc-server substitutes an always-failing Database, so a server with no index degrades to the pre-index behaviour.
- Drizzle's jsonb helper plus bun-sql double-encoded the media column, storing a JSON string rather than an array — readable, but opaque to every jsonb operator. Replaced with a customType that passes the value through and still parses old rows.
- Tail-built CDN URLs percent-encoded the DID and appended @jpeg, so a post indexed from the firehose got a different URL than the same post from a backfill. Now matches the appview exactly.
- actorByHandle now prefers the most recently confirmed row, since a handle can move between accounts and the index can briefly hold it on two DIDs.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED
- Decide whether mirroring like counts is worth the global like firehose (P2)
- Interested set has no eviction policy and will hit jetstream's 10k wantedDids cap (P2)
- Like tail holds every counted like URI in memory (P3)
- Reply and repost counts are frozen snapshots from backfill time (P3)
- Nothing ever re-walks a backfilled actor (P3)
- xrpc-server never retries the index after a failed DATABASE_URL at boot (P3)

Note: ratat-app-5p0 (cold deep jumps cost one upstream request per page) is now moot for backfilled actors but still applies to the live fallback path, so it stays open.

title: Phase 1: OAuth login + live artist pages from Bluesky appview + like/unlike
description:
Full plan: .hermes/plans/2026-08-05_ratat-lens-migration.md (Phase 1 section + decisions). Old repo for reference: /home/answer/Workspace/ratat.

Scope — first demoable milestone, no local Postgres index yet (that is Phase 2):

1. ATProto OAuth login in apps/web (TanStack Start). Port/adapt the old repo's OAuth flow (apps/frontend/src/app/oauth/, callback page, session handling). Check @atcute/* for current OAuth client packages before hand-rolling. Session must support server-side token use for PDS writes.
2. art.ratat.* query lexicons in packages/lexicon for the initial read surface (actor profile/portfolio feed), plus codegen (see ratat-app-8jg — wire @atcute/lex-cli as part of this if not done). Keep the surface minimal: roughly getActorProfile + getActorFeed.
3. apps/xrpc-server (Effect) implements those methods by proxying/hydrating LIVE from the public Bluesky appview (public.api.bsky.app): profile via app.bsky.actor.getProfile, portfolio via app.bsky.feed.getAuthorFeed with filter=posts_with_media. No reposts. Text-only posts invisible. Include video embeds.
4. Artist page in apps/web: /profile/:handle (match old repo routing conventions) — resolve handle, render portfolio as masonry grid (port ArtworkGrid/ArtworkCard patterns from old repo components), lightbox/detail view with images, alt text, like count, link out to Bluesky.
5. Like/unlike from the lightbox: writes a real app.bsky.feed.like via com.atproto.repo.createRecord/deleteRecord against the user's PDS using the OAuth session. One-time first-like notice ("likes are shared with Bluesky"). Like counts hydrate from the Bluesky appview.
6. Logged-out home = pure login page (already the placeholder). Logged-in home can be a stub pointing at profile search/visit for now — the real following feed is Phase 3.

Constraints: frontend must not use Effect; backend services must. Use tokens/light-dark() only (lint:colors gate). No posting UI, no boosts, no comments, no bookmarks, no collections. Identify users by DID. Quality gates: just check green + web build; exercise the XRPC methods against the live public appview.

Verification: log in with a real Bluesky account on the dev stack, visit an artist profile, see media-only portfolio, like + unlike a post and confirm the record appears/disappears in the repo (com.atproto.repo.listRecords).
close_reason:
Phase 1 shipped: OAuth login, live artist pages hydrated from the public Bluesky appview, and like/unlike writing real app.bsky.feed.like records. Commit 15510f5 on master.

WHAT WAS BUILT

packages/lexicon — @atcute/lex-cli codegen wired (closes ratat-app-8jg). Read surface kept to two methods: art.ratat.actor.getProfile and art.ratat.feed.getAuthorFeed, over art.ratat.actor.defs (profileViewBasic, profileView) and art.ratat.feed.defs (imageView, videoView, postView). Also authored art.ratat.graph.follow, the one locked custom record, for Phase 3.

packages/common — PUBLIC_BSKY_APPVIEW_URL, parseAtUri, bskyProfileUrl, bskyPostUrl; shared by both apps.

apps/xrpc-server (Effect) — @atcute/xrpc-server + @atcute/xrpc-server-bun, Bun.serve behind a ManagedRuntime, ported handler/runHandler/router shape from the old repo. An Appview layer wraps @atcute/client against BSKY_APPVIEW_URL (default https://public.api.bsky.app). getAuthorFeed requests filter=posts_with_media + includePins=false, then views.ts drops anything with reasonRepost and anything whose embed yields no media, so reposts and text-only posts are invisible. Images, video, and recordWithMedia all map into postView.media as a discriminated union.

apps/web (no Effect) — @atcute/oauth-browser-client, ported from the old frontend: loopback client_id on 127.0.0.1 in dev, a served /oauth/client-metadata.json (TanStack Start server route) elsewhere, /oauth/callback finalising the authorization. Session state is a small React context. /profile/$handle loads profile+portfolio in a route loader (so it server-renders), renders a CSS-column masonry grid, and opens a lightbox with all media, alt text, like button/count and a link out to Bluesky. Logged-out home is the login page; logged-in home is a handle-visit stub until Phase 3.

Like/unlike — com.atproto.repo.createRecord / deleteRecord against the user's PDS via the OAuth session. Viewer like state and fresh counts come from app.bsky.feed.getPosts routed through the user's PDS, because the public appview cannot return viewer state to an unauthenticated caller. A one-time notice ('liking here writes a real like to your Bluesky account') gates the first like and is remembered in localStorage.

KEY DECISIONS

1. Browser-held OAuth session, not server-side. The brief asked that the session support server-side token use. atcute's browser client binds the DPoP key to a non-extractable browser key, so those tokens cannot be replayed from the server at all; a server-side session needs a confidential client (@atcute/oauth-node-client), a keyset, and a session store that does not exist until packages/db lands in Phase 2. Phase 1's entire write surface is one like, issued from the browser, so browser-only is sufficient and much smaller. Filed ratat-app-bn7 to decide this properly when a real need appears.
2. Cursor pagination rather than the old repo's page/limit, because upstream getAuthorFeed is cursor-based and there is no local index to offset into. The lexicon documents that a page can be short or empty while a cursor remains, since media filtering happens after paging.
3. Viewer state fetched per-post on lightbox open rather than batched for the whole grid — one request instead of one per page, and the grid does not show liked state in Phase 1.
4. Generated lexicon output is committed and excluded from oxlint/oxfmt (packages/lexicon/lexicons/**), matching the old repo.
5. apps/web dev now binds 127.0.0.1 (not localhost), because the ATProto loopback client requires a 127.0.0.1 redirect URI; the home route also redirects localhost -> 127.0.0.1 in dev.

VERIFICATION

- Both XRPC methods exercised against the live public appview with curl: real profile fields for several accounts; media-only feeds with alt text, aspect ratios and like counts; videoView produced for nba.com and theonion.com; an unknown handle maps to HTTP 400 ProfileNotFound.
- app.bsky.feed.getPosts request shape (the like-state read) checked against the live appview with a throwaway script — returns likeCount, and viewer is absent unauthenticated as expected.
- Browser: SSR of /profile/bsky.app serves real CDN image URLs; the page and the lightbox render correctly (screenshots), the lightbox shows image + text + alt-text panel + like count + 'View on Bluesky', Escape/arrow keys and background scroll lock work, and no console errors beyond Vite/React dev notices.
- OAuth: sign-in from the login form completes the PAR handshake with bsky.social and lands on the Bluesky sign-in page with the identifier prefilled, which exercises client metadata, DPoP key generation and pushed authorization.
- Quality gates: 'just check' (lint, lint-colors, format-check, typecheck) and 'bun run build' both green.

NOT VERIFIED — the issue's verification step asks for a real login plus a like/unlike round-trip confirmed via com.atproto.repo.listRecords. That needs a real Bluesky account password, which I do not have, so the flow is verified only up to the PDS authorization page. The write path is a direct port of the old repo's working createRecord/deleteRecord code with the collection swapped to app.bsky.feed.like. Please run that last check once when convenient.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: ratat-app-qj3 (HLS video only plays natively in Safari; the lightbox currently renders the .m3u8 playlist directly), ratat-app-bn7 (server-side OAuth session decision), ratat-app-4pu (caching and 429 handling for appview hydration).

title: Honour the signed-in viewer's Bluesky mutes and blocks
description:
The migration plan's moderation section asks for the viewer's own mutes and blocks to be respected via hydrated viewer state when logged in. Phase 4 shipped only the device-local label filter, which is a different thing: somebody who blocked an account on Bluesky still sees their work in a Ratat feed.

Needs an authenticated read path — the xrpc-server currently talks to the public appview with no session — or a client-side pass using the viewer's own agent against app.bsky.graph.getMutes / getBlocks, cached in the web app the way follows are.

Filed from Phase 4 (ratat-app-6ua).

title: Refresh moderation labels on indexed posts
description:
A post's labels enter the index only on a hydrated write — the backfill. A labeler that acts on a post after Ratat indexed it never reaches the index, so a work labelled today keeps serving with the labels it had when it was first read. The live read path (getPost against an un-backfilled actor) is fine; the indexed path is the gap.

Options: subscribe to com.atproto.label.subscribeLabels for the labelers we honour and patch post.labels on the fly; or re-hydrate labels on a schedule for recently-read posts; or fall back to a per-request appview hydration for posts whose labels are older than N days.

Filed from Phase 4 (ratat-app-6ua), where labels were first carried end to end.

title: Verify the OAuth follow write path in a browser
description:
Phase 3 verified everything around the follow write except the write itself: creating and deleting an art.ratat.graph.follow through the app needs an interactive OAuth login, which was not available in the Phase 3 session. Verified instead: the graph walk against a real PDS, the tail's create/delete handler against real Postgres, the timeline read, and the import batching by unit test.

To close: sign in at 127.0.0.1:3000, follow an artist from a profile page, watch the row appear in ratat_follow via the jetstream follows tail (not the walk), unfollow, watch it go. Then run the import-follows onboarding once against a test account and confirm the applyWrites batches land.

title: Prioritise Ratat-followed artists in the backfill queue
description:
The post-backfill worker takes the oldest interested DID first, so an artist somebody just Ratat-followed waits behind everything already queued. Measured during Phase 3: a 26,521-artwork walk of a news bot held the queue for over two minutes, and five freshly followed artists sat behind two such accounts until their interested_at was bumped by hand. A newly imported follow graph therefore shows an empty home feed for minutes.

Options: order the queue by trigger (a ratat-follow subject before a profile visitor), or cap a single walk's pages so one prolific account cannot monopolise the worker, or run a second worker for follow-triggered targets. Documented as a limit in docs/architecture/indexing.md.

title: Decide whether mirroring like counts is worth the global like firehose
description:
The plan's 2026-08-06 decision mirrors like_count into the index instead of hydrating it live, on the grounds that live per-read hydration is too expensive. Phase 2 implements that.

The cost is not symmetric with the reasoning, and it should be looked at again with real numbers. A like lives in the *liker's* repo, so the subscription cannot be scoped by DID the way the post tail is: it is the entire app.bsky.feed.like firehose — measured at ~210 events/second, every one of them decoded and thrown away. Local filtering is cheap (one at-uri parse plus a set lookup), but the bandwidth is not.

The alternative that was displaced — batching getPosts hydration behind the cache in ratat-app-4pu — costs one upstream request per ~25 posts *per read*, which at Ratat's traffic may well be less than a permanent firehose.

JETSTREAM_LIKE_TAIL=false already turns the tail off; counts then hold at their backfilled values.
acceptance_criteria: A measured comparison of firehose bandwidth against cached hydration traffic, and a recorded decision.
close_reason: Decided: keep the global like tail. ~210 ev/s decode cost is acceptable — likes are cheap compared to posts. Likes never mark DIDs interested or trigger backfill (subject-filtered only), which was the actual concern. JETSTREAM_LIKE_TAIL stays default-on.

title: Interested set has no eviction policy and will hit jetstream's 10k wantedDids cap
description:
Every profile visit adds a DID to the interested set and nothing ever removes one. Jetstream refuses to scope a subscription to more than 10,000 DIDs; past that the tail logs an error and silently drops events from the overflow, so those actors' pages quietly go stale while still being served from the index as if current.

Needs an eviction or tiering policy: drop actors with no recent reads, or split the tail across several subscriptions, or fall back to an unscoped post firehose past a threshold. Documented under 'Limits' in docs/architecture/indexing.md.
acceptance_criteria: The tail keeps working correctly past 10k interested DIDs, or the set is bounded so it cannot get there.

title: xrpc-server exits silently when it cannot bind its port
description:
apps/xrpc-server/src/main.ts runs the server with Effect.runFork. If Bun.serve fails — most commonly EADDRINUSE because another process already holds PORT — the fiber dies, nothing is logged, and the process exits with status 0. It looks exactly like a clean start followed by an immediate clean shutdown.

Found while verifying Phase 2 (ratat-app-0co): a stray service on port 3002 made the server exit silently, which read at first like a database-layer bug. Cost real debugging time.

Fix: surface the fiber's exit — log the cause and exit non-zero when the serve fiber fails, rather than dropping it. Same applies to apps/ingester/src/main.ts.

title: getAuthorFeed page walking: cold deep jumps cost one upstream request per page
description:
art.ratat.feed.getAuthorFeed reaches ?page=N by walking upstream cursors. apps/xrpc-server/src/cursor-cache.ts memoises the cursor that starts each page (5 min TTL, 5000 entries, in-process), so Next/Prev/revisits and any page an earlier walk crossed cost one upstream request. A cold jump — first visitor, after a restart, or after the TTL — still costs one request per page walked, up to the lexicon ceiling of page=100.

Limits worth removing later: the cache is per-process (not shared between instances and lost on restart), and its entries go stale when new posts shift page boundaries, which can duplicate or skip a post at a boundary. The Phase 2 Postgres index makes this moot by paginating on an offset/keyset over indexed posts; until then, consider a shared cache or a lower page ceiling if the walk shows up in latency.
acceptance_criteria: Deep page jumps do not fan out to one upstream request per page, or the walk is replaced by index-backed pagination.

title: Profile pager total is Bluesky postsCount, not art-post count
description:
The profile pager sizes its page slots from profile.postsCount and renders it as a capped total ('804+ works'). postsCount counts every post the account made; the art feed only carries posts with media, so the estimate can overshoot badly — bsky.app shows '804+ works' on page 1 but the feed really holds 169 across 6 pages. Users see page numbers and a Last link for pages that do not exist; the numbers only become exact once they reach the end of the feed.

The appview cannot count art posts without an index, so this is a Phase 2 (Postgres index) fix: count media posts per author and return an exact total from art.ratat.feed.getAuthorFeed, then drop the postsCount estimate in apps/web/src/routes/profile.$handle.tsx (paginationFor).
acceptance_criteria: Profile pager shows an exact work count and an accurate page count without walking to the end of the feed.

title: Cache and rate-limit-guard public appview hydration in xrpc-server
description: apps/xrpc-server proxies every art.ratat.actor.getProfile and art.ratat.feed.getAuthorFeed straight through to https://public.api.bsky.app with no caching. Risk 3 in .hermes/plans/2026-08-05_ratat-lens-migration.md: bursty portfolio paging will draw 429s, and today a 429 surfaces to the client as a bare UpstreamFailure. Add a small per-instance response cache keyed by (method, actor, cursor) with a short TTL, and map upstream 429/5xx onto retry-aware XRPC errors.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated identical profile/feed requests inside the TTL hit the cache, and an upstream 429 produces a distinguishable error rather than a generic UpstreamFailure.

title: Decide whether PDS writes need a server-side OAuth session
description: Phase 1 uses @atcute/oauth-browser-client: the OAuth session and its DPoP key live in the browser, and likes are written straight from the browser to the user's PDS. That satisfies the Phase 1 write surface but means no server-side code can act as the user — a DPoP-bound token tied to a non-extractable browser key cannot be replayed from the xrpc-server. If a later phase needs server-side writes or server-rendered viewer state (e.g. hydrating viewer.like during SSR instead of a client fetch), we need a confidential client: @atcute/oauth-node-client plus a keyset, confidential client metadata, and a server session store (which lands with packages/db in Phase 2). Evaluate then; do not build it speculatively.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision: keep browser-only sessions, or a plan for the confidential-client migration including where sessions are stored.

title: Play HLS video embeds outside Safari
description: The lightbox renders app.bsky.embed.video as <video src={playlist}> where playlist is an HLS .m3u8 manifest. Only Safari plays HLS natively; Chrome and Firefox show the poster and fail to play. Phase 1 shipped this knowingly (see apps/web/src/components/Lightbox.tsx MediaFrame). Either attach hls.js when the browser lacks native HLS support, or fall back to a poster with a play affordance that opens the post on Bluesky.
acceptance_criteria: A video post in an artist portfolio plays inline in Chromium, or degrades to an explicit poster+link fallback rather than a broken player.

title: Wire @atcute/lex-cli codegen in packages/lexicon
description: packages/lexicon is an empty placeholder (src/index.ts exports nothing, lexicons/ is a .gitkeep). Once art.ratat.graph.follow and the art.ratat.* query lexicons are authored, wire @atcute/lex-cli generate/export the way the old repo does and re-export the generated types.
acceptance_criteria: 'bun run --cwd packages/lexicon generate' produces types from lexicons/*.json and typecheck passes.
close_reason: Wired @atcute/lex-cli codegen in packages/lexicon. lex.config.ts generates from lexicons-src/**/*.ts into lexicons/ with imports [@atcute/atproto, @atcute/bluesky]; 'bun run --cwd packages/lexicon generate' emits lexicons/index.ts plus lexicons/types/art/ratat/**. Authored art.ratat.actor.defs, art.ratat.actor.getProfile, art.ratat.feed.defs, art.ratat.feed.getAuthorFeed and the one custom record art.ratat.graph.follow (unused until Phase 3, but it is the locked custom lexicon and the generator input the issue named). src/index.ts re-exports ../lexicons/index.ts plus src/collections.ts (nsid constants); package exports expose '.' and './collections'. Generated output is committed and excluded from oxlint/oxfmt via 'packages/lexicon/lexicons/**' ignorePatterns, matching the old repo. Note the acceptance criterion said 'types from lexicons/*.json' — atcute's lex-cli takes TypeScript builder documents as input, not JSON, so the source of truth is lexicons-src/*.ts and 'lex-cli export' is the script that emits JSON. Verified: generate runs clean and 'bun run --cwd packages/lexicon typecheck' passes; the generated schemas are consumed by apps/xrpc-server (router + handlers) and apps/web (typed client).

title: Add Effect Database layer to packages/db
description: packages/db currently exports only the raw drizzle client and migration runner. The Effect services (xrpc-server, ingester) need the Database context tag / DbError / DatabaseLive layer pattern from the old repo's packages/db/src/effect.ts. Port it when the first service actually reads from Postgres (Phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: @ratat/db exposes an './effect' entrypoint with Database, DbError and DatabaseLive; a backend service consumes it.
close_reason:
Implemented as part of ratat-app-0co (Phase 2). packages/db now exposes ./effect with Database, DbError and DatabaseLive, ported from the old repo's packages/db/src/effect.ts.

One deliberate change from the port: DatabaseLive is typed Layer<Database, DbError> rather than Layer<Database>. The old version used Effect.promise, so a missing DATABASE_URL surfaced as a defect. Typing it as an ordinary failure is what lets apps/xrpc-server decide what to do about it — it substitutes a Database whose every query fails, and the read paths already treat a DbError as 'serve live from Bluesky instead'. A server with no database configured degrades to the pre-index behaviour and logs a warning, rather than 500ing every request.

The layer deliberately does not open a connection when it is built. Postgres being down is then a per-query DbError, which each read falls back on and which recovers by itself once Postgres returns.

Both apps/xrpc-server and apps/ingester consume it.

title: Set up Tailwind v4 + light-dark() token system + lint:colors gate in apps/web
description: apps/web was scaffolded blank (plain CSS in src/styles.css) to keep Phase 0 minimal. The old repo styles with Tailwind v4 and a globals.css light-dark() token system, enforced by a 'lint:colors' script (apps/frontend/scripts/check-color-literals.ts) wired into the root gates and lint-staged. Port that before building real UI.
acceptance_criteria: Tailwind v4 builds in apps/web; globals.css token system ported; 'bun run lint:colors' exists at the root and is part of 'just check'.
close_reason: Tailwind v4 wired into apps/web via @tailwindcss/vite (Vite plugin route, replacing the old repo's Next/PostCSS integration). Ported the full light-dark() token set, @custom-variant dark, @theme inline mapping and @layer base from apps/frontend/src/app/globals.css into apps/web/src/styles.css, keeping every token name. Dropped only the @layer components block, the tw-animate-css import and the base-ui data-open/data-closed variants — all component styling for gallery/upload UI that does not exist here (follow-up ratat-app-cso). Ported scripts/check-color-literals.ts, retargeting GLOBALS_CSS to src/styles.css; wired 'lint:colors' at apps/web and root, plus a 'lint-colors' recipe inside 'just check'. Login placeholder restyled with tokens only. Verified: bun install, just check green, negative test of the colour gate fails as expected, vite build emits compiled utilities, and dev server serves the styles with lightningcss lowering light-dark() correctly for both prefers-color-scheme and data-theme. Follow-ups: ratat-app-263, ratat-app-cso.

title: Port testnet harness + mise/pitchfork dev-stack wiring
description: Phase 0 step 3 was deferred: ratat-app has docker-compose (Postgres only) and a justfile, but no local ATProto testnet. Port packages/testnet, mise.toml, and pitchfork.toml from ~/Workspace/ratat, keeping the port-offset conventions from that repo's AGENTS.md, so 'pitchfork start -l' boots the full stack.
acceptance_criteria: pitchfork start -l boots web, xrpc-server, ingester, Postgres and the testnet PDS/PLC/relay; just up/down manage both compose files.

title: Phase 4: label-based content filtering + quick settings, actor typeahead, polish, quality gates
description:
Full plan: .hermes/plans/2026-08-05_ratat-lens-migration.md (Phase 4 section + Decisions). Old repo reference for DESIGN ONLY: /home/answer/Workspace/ratat/apps/frontend — port designs 1:1 per CLAUDE.md (square corners, old layout, quick-settings/theming look; never invent designs).

Goal: moderation, search, and final polish — the last planned phase.

Scope:
1. Label-based content filtering: hydrate moderation labels for posts/actors from Bluesky (labels come through the public appview post/profile views; also label snapshot already stored on indexed posts — extend if needed). Device-local filter preferences (localStorage): per-label-group settings (e.g. adult content show/warn/hide) matching Bluesky's standard label values (porn, sexual, nudity, graphic-media, etc.). Default: warn/blur for adult labels. Blurred cards get a click-through reveal; port the old app's blur/warning card design if it had one, otherwise the minimal square-cornered equivalent consistent with the design system.
2. Quick settings: port the old app's quick-settings UI (the Settings cog popover already partially exists on the Pager — extend per old design) to include the content-filter toggles + existing "Always show details" toggle. Settings are device-local; no server persistence.
3. Actor typeahead search: the masthead search box currently only navigates to a handle. Port the old app's typeahead design: as-you-type suggestions via app.bsky.actor.searchActorsTypeahead proxied through xrpc-server (art.ratat.actor.searchActorsTypeahead query lexicon, thin proxy), keyboard navigation, enter-to-go.
4. Polish: empty states (empty home feed for new users pointing at onboarding/import, empty profile, artwork not found), error states (bad handle, unreachable appview), loading states — all designed per old app where a reference exists.
5. Logged-out home: confirm it stays the pure login page (already true) and looks 1:1 like the old login design.
6. Quality gates hardening: ensure just check covers lint, lint:colors, format, typecheck across all workspaces; add an e2e smoke script (scripts/ or justfile target) that starts the stack and curls key endpoints (getProfile, getAuthorFeed, getTimeline, getPost, searchActorsTypeahead) asserting 200 + shape. Do NOT port the testnet harness (separate issue ratat-app-uuk).

Constraints: frontend no Effect; backend all Effect; colors only via light-dark() tokens; device-local moderation prefs only (no account settings server-side); do NOT push; no narrating comments.

Gates: just check green, cd apps/web && bun run build green, e2e smoke green, and browser verification: typeahead suggests real actors and navigates; a known-NSFW-labeled post (find one via search on Bluesky) renders blurred with working reveal and the hide setting removes it; quick settings toggles persist across reload. Document verification results in the close reason.

title: Dev servers started from a package directory get no DATABASE_URL
description:
bun loads .env from the process cwd, and .env lives at the repo root. Starting the xrpc-server with 'cd apps/xrpc-server && bun run dev' therefore gives it no DATABASE_URL: the Database layer degrades to the 'index unavailable' stub, every read silently falls back to the live Bluesky path, and getTimeline — which has no live fallback — answers 502 UpstreamFailure.

It looks like a broken timeline rather than a missing env var, which is how it survived until the Phase 4 smoke test hit it. 'just dev' is fine (dotenv-load), so this only bites somebody starting one service by hand.

Fix options: a per-app .env that points at the root one, an explicit dotenv load in each app's config, or a boot-time hard failure when DATABASE_URL is absent instead of the silent degrade (the degrade is deliberate for production, so probably a loud warning naming the variable).

Filed from Phase 4 (ratat-app-6ua).
notes: Related to ratat-app-f0w, which covers the other half: once the environment is fixed, the xrpc-server still needs a restart because the degraded Database layer is sticky for the life of the process.

title: Search is unreachable below 880px
description:
The masthead search box carries max-[880px]:hidden, ported from the old app, so a narrow window has no way to find an artist at all — there is no mobile search affordance behind it. The old app had the same hole; the typeahead work in Phase 4 did not close it.

Wants a design decision first: a search icon that expands over the masthead, or a dedicated /search route the icon links to.

Filed from Phase 4 (ratat-app-6ua).

title: Carry account labels on bylines so cards can honour them
description:
art.ratat.actor.defs#profileView carries labels and the profile header covers the banner and avatar with them. profileViewBasic — the byline on every post view — does not, so an account-level label (an adult account whose individual posts carry no label) covers nothing in a feed or a timeline.

Doing it properly means storing account labels on the actor row, since indexed reads build bylines from that snapshot rather than from a live profile fetch. That is a schema column plus a refresh story, which is why Phase 4 stopped at the profile header.

Filed from Phase 4 (ratat-app-6ua).

title: Artwork detail: carousel for multi-image posts instead of stacked rows
description:
## Context `apps/web/src/routes/art.$handle.$rkey.tsx` currently renders every item in `post.media` as its own full-height row: ```tsx {post.media.map((media, index) => (
))} ``` `MediaFrame` is `height: calc(100vh - 260px)`, so a Bluesky post carrying multiple images (up to 4 per the images embed) becomes a long vertical scroll of near-viewport-tall frames. Single-image posts are fine. ## Desired change When `post.media.length > 1`, render the artwork in a **carousel** instead of stacked rows: one media frame at a time, with prev/next controls and an index indicator. Single-media posts keep the current rendering unchanged. Notes: - A video embed is always a single `MediaView` (see `packages/common/src/media.ts`), so a carousel only ever contains images in practice; the video case should just not appear in carousel mode. - The old app's `ArtworkDetail` (`~/Workspace/ratat/apps/frontend/src/components/art/ArtworkDetail.tsx`) only ever rendered a single artwork image — there is **no carousel to port 1:1** from it. Design one consistent with the ported UI conventions: square corners, `var(--...)` tokens (e.g. `--ink-raised`, `--line`, `--paper`), and the numbered-pager style already used by `Pager.tsx` for index display. ## Acceptance criteria - Multi-image artwork detail shows one image at a time with working prev/next navigation and a visible index (e.g. "2 / 4"), matching the old app's numbered-pager aesthetic. - Single-image posts and video posts render exactly as they do today. - No new dependencies unless genuinely needed; keyboard arrow support is a nice-to-have. - Quality gates pass: repo typecheck/lint/tests.

title: Re-read a Ratat follow graph after the one-off walk
description:
follows_backfilled_at is stamped once and never cleared, so the graph walk of a repo happens exactly once. If the follows tail is down while somebody follows an artist, that follow is missing from the index until the record is rewritten — the walk will not pick it up again, and the timeline silently omits that artist.

Cheap fix: clear follows_backfilled_at on a schedule, or re-walk when the tail reconnects after a gap longer than its cursor retention.

title: xrpc-server never retries the index after a failed DATABASE_URL at boot
description:
apps/xrpc-server/src/runtime.ts degrades to an always-failing Database when DatabaseLive cannot be built (missing or malformed DATABASE_URL), which is the right call: reads fall back to live rather than 500ing. But the stub is permanent for the life of the process — fixing the environment needs a restart.

Postgres merely being *down* is handled better: those are per-query failures that recover by themselves once it returns. Only the layer-construction path is sticky.

Low priority: the trigger is a misconfiguration, and the symptom is a loud warning plus correct-but-slower behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: Either the layer is rebuilt on a later request, or the sticky degradation is a documented, deliberate choice.

title: Nothing ever re-walks a backfilled actor
description:
Backfill is a single point-in-time walk: once backfilled_at is stamped, the actor is never re-read from the appview. A page missed mid-walk (an appview hiccup, a rate limit, the BACKFILL_MAX_PAGES cap) leaves a permanent hole that only a manual 'update actor set backfilled_at = null' fixes.

The tail keeps new posts current, so the hole is always in the past — which is exactly where a portfolio's best work usually is.

Wants a re-backfill trigger: a staleness threshold, an admin path, or a cheap 'is the newest indexed post still the newest post' probe on read.
acceptance_criteria: A gap in an indexed portfolio can be repaired without hand-editing Postgres.

title: Reply and repost counts are frozen snapshots from backfill time
description:
post.reply_count and post.repost_count are seeded when a post is indexed and never updated: ArtworkCard and the artwork page render whatever the numbers were at backfill. A post indexed by the jetstream tail shows 0/0 forever.

Maintaining them the way like_count is maintained means two more global firehose tails (app.bsky.feed.repost, and app.bsky.feed.post filtered on reply.parent), which is a lot of bandwidth for two small numbers. A cheaper option is a periodic getPosts refresh for recently-read posts.

Decide whether these numbers are worth anything; if not, drop them from the card.
acceptance_criteria: Either the counts are maintained, refreshed periodically, or removed from the UI.

title: Like tail holds every counted like URI in memory
description:
apps/ingester/src/tail.ts loads the whole post_like table into a Set at boot, so a like delete — which arrives from jetstream with no record and therefore no subject — can be recognised without querying Postgres for every delete on the network.

The set is bounded by our own index rather than by Bluesky, but nothing else bounds it: roughly 80 bytes per like, so a million likes on indexed posts is ~80MB of resident memory plus a full table scan at every boot.

Options: a bloom filter in front of the query, sharding by rkey prefix, or dropping like rows older than some window and accepting slow upward drift on old posts.
acceptance_criteria: Like-delete attribution no longer needs the whole table resident.

title: Pager: URL page can outrun the page actually served
description:
Asking for a page past the end of a feed (e.g. /profile/bsky.app?page=27 when the feed holds 6 pages) serves the last page and the pager correctly highlights page 6, but the URL still reads ?page=27. Bookmarking or sharing that URL keeps the mismatch, and the browser history holds a page number that does not exist.

Fix by having the route redirect/replace to the served page (portfolio.page) when it differs from the requested one, once TanStack redirect-in-loader interplay with SSR is settled.
acceptance_criteria: Landing on a page past the end leaves the URL naming the page actually shown.

title: Artwork detail: port comments, tags, collections and boost
description: The /art/$handle/$rkey page ports ArtworkDetail's layout but omits the parts with no backend: Comments, TagPill list, collection chips, boost/report buttons, license and edited notices. Fill these in as the corresponding lexicons land.
acceptance_criteria: detail page matches components/art/ArtworkDetail.tsx section for section

title: Guard against --spacing-* tokens shadowing Tailwind container widths
description: The ported theme defines --spacing-xs/sm/md/lg/xl/xxl. Tailwind v4 resolves max-w-*/w-*/min-w-* from both --container-* and --spacing-*, so max-w-md silently compiled to 12px and collapsed the login page (fixed in ratat-app-6e7 by dropping the t-shirt widths). Nothing stops it recurring. Options: extend apps/web/scripts to reject max-w-/min-w-/w- with xs|sm|md|lg|xl|xxl suffixes, or rename the spacing tokens.
acceptance_criteria: a reintroduced max-w-md fails a repo check

title: Profile page: port remaining tabs and ProfileSidebar
description: ProfileHeader ports the old design but only the Art tab exists: Collections, Boosts, Favourites and Bluesky have no appview queries. ProfileSidebar (You may also like / More like this) is omitted for the same reason — the .layout/.feed shell is already in place for it. Also missing: FollowButton, owner edit mode, banner connection links.
acceptance_criteria: profile page renders the old app's full TabNav and sidebar rails

title: Masthead: add Following nav item and SearchBar when their routes exist
description: MastheadNav currently renders only Home because apps/web has no /following route, and HandleSearch stands in for the old app's SearchBar (typeahead, tag/actor chips, search-query parsing). Restore both against the old app's components once a following feed and a search query land.
acceptance_criteria: MastheadNav matches components/MastheadNav.tsx; search input matches components/search/SearchBar.tsx
close_reason: Both halves resolved rather than done. SearchBar landed in Phase 4 (ratat-app-6ua): apps/web/src/components/search/SearchBar.tsx ports the old app's frame, dropdown and keyboard handling, with the tag and operator halves left out because v1 searches actors only (plan decision: 'Search: actor typeahead only'). The Following nav item is cut, not pending — the plan's round-2 decisions retire the old top-nav Following page and rail in favour of home being the ratat-follow timeline.

title: Re-add tw-animate-css + base-ui data-open/data-closed variants when component UI lands
description: ratat-app-eds ported the token layer of the old globals.css but dropped the 'tw-animate-css' import and the '@custom-variant data-open/data-closed' declarations, since both only serve @base-ui/react component styling that does not exist in apps/web yet. It also dropped the old '@layer components' block (.wrap, .brand, .btn, .piece, .masonry, .act, actor-typeahead) because those style deleted gallery/upload UI. Re-add the pieces that are still wanted when real component UI is built.
acceptance_criteria: component-layer styling decision made when the first shared components land in apps/web
close_reason: Ported the old globals.css @layer components block into apps/web/src/styles.css as part of ratat-app-6e7: .wrap, .brand/.brand__mark, .btn + accent/ghost/danger variants, .gallery/.layout/.feed, .masonry, the whole .piece family, and .act. Skipped actor-typeahead (no such component in this app). Decision on the other two dropped pieces: tw-animate-css and the @custom-variant data-open/data-closed declarations stay out — they only serve @base-ui/react, and the ported components use plain conditional rendering instead. Revisit if base-ui is ever adopted.

title: Port theming docs + lint-staged colour gate from old repo
description: The old repo documented the token system in docs/frontend/theming.md and ran 'lint:colors' as a lint-staged pre-commit hook on apps/frontend/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}. Neither was ported with ratat-app-eds: this repo has no docs/ tree and no husky/lint-staged setup yet, so the colour gate only runs via 'just check'. Port the theming doc and, if pre-commit hooks are wanted here, wire the gate into them.
acceptance_criteria: docs describing the light-dark() token system exist in this repo; decision recorded on whether pre-commit hooks are used, and gate wired in if so

title: Add husky + lint-staged pre-commit hooks
description: The old repo runs oxfmt/oxlint --fix on staged JS/TS and oxfmt on staged json/css/md via husky + lint-staged. ratat-app has the same lint/format gates but no pre-commit hook, so formatting drift only surfaces in 'just check'.
acceptance_criteria: Committing an unformatted file triggers oxfmt/oxlint automatically.
